categoryNote: Foundational category - implemented first. It creates and preserves the recovery substrate that every other category depends on. This file is the single source of truth for NX16; the playbook build is generated from it.

tweaks.name: System Restore enablement & configuration
tweaks.description: Enables System Restore protection on the system drive with a sane disk allocation.
tweaks.objective: Guarantee an OS-level recovery anchor exists before NEXTRIX changes anything.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Removes DisableSR/DisableRPC policy values if present (journaled), enables protection via Enable-ComputerRestore on the system drive, and sets a disk allocation the user selects (default 2-6 GB). NEXTRIX never deletes restore points or shadow copies (inversion of the reference pattern that sabotages recovery, PROJECT_RESEARCH).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: System Restore often disabled on fresh Windows 11 installs.
tweaks.proposedState: Protection enabled on the system drive with user-selected allocation.

verify.procedure: Get-ComputerRestorePoint lists points and protection is enabled for the system drive.

rollback.procedure: Disable-ComputerRestore for the system drive; prior policy values restored from journal.

originalState.method: DisableSR/DisableRPC policy values and prior protection state captured to journal before change.

sideEffects: Disk space consumed by restore points within the chosen allocation.

tweaks.name: Pre-change restore point creation ritual
tweaks.description: Creates a System Restore point immediately before the first mutation of every apply session.
tweaks.objective: A second, OS-level safety net behind the journal, taken before any change.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Temporarily sets SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency=0 (value captured first, restored after), then Checkpoint-Computer -RestorePointType MODIFY_SETTINGS. Handles the Windows 24h throttle honestly: if creation is throttled but a point newer than 24h exists, keeps the existing point instead of failing (SynToolkit/UltraOS pattern). Never deletes shadows.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX restore point; Windows cadence unchanged.
tweaks.proposedState: Restore point 'NEXTRIX pre-apply <timestamp>' exists for the session.

verify.procedure: Get-ComputerRestorePoint returns a point newer than session start, or an existing <24h point was intentionally kept (reported).

rollback.procedure: Additive only - NEXTRIX never deletes restore points; the temporary frequency override is restored from journal.

originalState.method: SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency prior value captured and restored (UltraOS L0 pattern, r4).

sideEffects: Brief VSS activity during point creation.

tweaks.name: Targeted registry backup
tweaks.description: Exports every registry key family NEXTRIX is about to touch, before touching it.
tweaks.objective: File-level, hand-importable copies of the exact pre-change state.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: reg.exe export of each distinct key path referenced by the session's selected tweaks to %ProgramData%\NEXTRIX\Backups\<timestamp>\, with an index manifest. This is defense-in-depth behind the journal (journal restores precisely; .reg exports are human-readable and hand-importable).
tweaks.proposedState: Timestamped backup set covering all session target keys.

verify.procedure: Backup set exists and every selected tweak's key path has a .reg file listed in the index manifest.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - backup is additive; files are importable by the user if ever needed.

originalState.method: The backup IS the original-state artifact for the covered keys.

tweaks.name: Pre-flight original-state snapshot bundle
tweaks.description: Journal initialization plus hardware/build reports and the NX16-002/003/005/006 backups, run as one ritual before the first mutation.
tweaks.objective: One gate that proves capture completeness BEFORE anything is changed (no mutation without verified prior state).
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Initializes the journal (capture-refusal if a previous NEXTRIX journal exists unresolved), writes hardware.json/build.json reports, then invokes the backup functions. If any capture step fails, the apply session refuses to continue - destructive steps are gated on capture completeness (XOS event-channel gate pattern, r1).
tweaks.proposedState: Journal armed + reports + backup set complete and verified.

verify.procedure: Pre-flight report shows all capture steps Complete; journal manifest present; no Failed steps.

sideEffects: Disk usage for reports and backups.

tweaks.name: Service configuration backup
tweaks.description: Exports the startup type and running state of every service NEXTRIX may touch in the session.
tweaks.objective: Whole-state service baseline, beyond per-change journal entries.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Enumerates HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services Start values plus current status via Get-Service for the session's target services; writes a validated .reg export plus a JSON baseline. First backup is never overwritten (Atlas pattern, r2).
tweaks.proposedState: Baseline .reg + JSON covering session target services.

verify.procedure: Baseline files exist and enumerate every session target service.

tweaks.name: Scheduled task backup
tweaks.description: Exports the XML and state of every scheduled task NEXTRIX may touch in the session.
tweaks.objective: Whole-state task baseline for exact restoration.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: For each session target task: Export-ScheduledTask XML plus current State into the timestamped backup set. Restoring a task is therefore a documented import, not a reconstruction.
tweaks.proposedState: Task XML + state baseline covering session targets.

verify.procedure: Backup set contains one XML + state record per session target task.

tweaks.name: DISM health check & repair tooling
tweaks.description: Runs DISM CheckHealth/ScanHealth; repair (RestoreHealth) is owner-initiated only.
tweaks.objective: Know whether the component store is healthy before and after configuration changes.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: CheckHealth is instant and read-only; ScanHealth is deeper and read-only; RestoreHealth is never run automatically - the report proposes it as an owner action. Read-only by default: no mutation without consent.
tweaks.proposedState: DISM health report generated on demand and in the support bundle.

verify.procedure: Report shows CheckHealth/ScanHealth output with a clear health verdict.

tweaks.name: SFC verification tooling
tweaks.description: Runs sfc /verifyonly as the default integrity check; repair is owner-initiated only.
tweaks.objective: Detect system-file integrity issues without automatically changing anything.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: sfc /verifyonly is the read-only form. NEXTRIX deliberately does NOT refuse sfc /scannow (contrast: ame-sfc-interface warns against it, r6) - the support bundle simply reports what it finds and proposes the owner command.
tweaks.proposedState: SFC verify report available on demand.

tweaks.name: Component store cleanup (on-demand)
tweaks.description: Runs DISM StartComponentCleanup on explicit request only; /ResetBase is never used.
tweaks.objective: Reclaim component-store space on demand without sacrificing update removability.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: StartComponentCleanup removes superseded component versions but keeps installed updates uninstallable. /ResetBase permanently removes that ability (WinUtil rejected pattern, r5) and is excluded by design. Never scheduled silently - explicit run only.
tweaks.defaultState: Component store grows with servicing; Windows scheduled task handles it slowly over time.
tweaks.proposedState: Component store trimmed on demand; updates remain uninstallable-capable.

verify.procedure: DISM completes successfully; store size reported before/after.

rollback.procedure: Not reversible per-component; the operation is a documented, explicit one-way trim (honest labeling - not disguised as reversible).

originalState.method: Not applicable - store maintenance; size before/after recorded in the report.

sideEffects: Takes several minutes; temporary elevated CPU/disk usage.

tweaks.name: Driver inventory & history report
tweaks.description: Read-only inventory of installed drivers with dates, versions and providers.
tweaks.objective: Evidence base for driver decisions and the support bundle.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: CIM Win32_PnPSignedDriver enumeration plus DriverStore usage stats; read-only. Feeds NX20-008/009 later; driver removal remains separate from optimization per directive.
tweaks.proposedState: Driver inventory report available on demand.

tweaks.name: Driver Store selective cleanup
tweaks.description: Removes orphaned Driver Store packages that pnputil marks unused, per-package with explicit consent.
tweaks.objective: Reclaim Driver Store space without touching in-use drivers.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Lists Driver Store packages via pnputil /enum-drivers, cross-checks in-use status, and proposes only orphaned packages for deletion - each individually confirmed, never a blanket sweep. A pre-action backup of the package list is journaled; deletion of a driver package is honestly labeled NOT reversible via journal (reinstall media required).
tweaks.defaultState: Driver Store retains old driver versions after upgrades.
tweaks.proposedState: User-confirmed orphaned packages removed; inventory recorded before/after.

verify.procedure: pnputil enum no longer lists the removed orphaned packages; in-use drivers untouched.

rollback.procedure: Honest labeling: driver-package deletion is NOT journal-reversible; the before/after inventory and original .inf names are recorded for manual reinstall.

originalState.method: Full package enumeration exported to the backup set before any deletion.

sideEffects: Removing the wrong package can break a device - hence per-package consent and orphan-only scope.

tweaks.name: Windows build & UBR verification report
tweaks.description: Read-only report of edition, build, UBR, architecture, marketing version and scope status.
tweaks.objective: The build context every tweak gate consumes; also owner-facing verification.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-NxBuildReport (src/nxcore/NxBuild.ps1): registry CurrentVersion read with explicit Failed/Uncertain sentinels, ADR-003 scope check (22631..26300), Insider-channel flag, 24H2 caution flag. Capability detection remains the primary gate per directive Section 10.

tweaks.name: Individual tweak rollback
tweaks.description: Restores the exact recorded original state of one tweak (registry scope in engine v0.1).
tweaks.objective: Scope 1 of 4: undo a single selected change precisely.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId (src/nxcore/NxRollback.ps1): reads the journal, verifies the integrity chain, reverses apply entries in reverse order, restores exact original values/kinds, deletes values that never existed, refuses on integrity errors, and honors only-if-ours - divergence is reported, never clobbered. Every rollback step is itself journaled and verified.
tweaks.proposedState: Tweak's recorded targets restored to their exact original states.

verify.procedure: Rollback result object: restored targets verified; diverged/failed lists empty or explained.

rollback.procedure: Rollback steps are journaled; applying the tweak again re-journals a new original.

originalState.method: Restores the journal-recorded original (never guessed Windows defaults).

tweaks.name: Category rollback
tweaks.description: Restores all journaled changes for one category (e.g. all NX02 entries).
tweaks.objective: Scope 2 of 4: category-level undo with identical semantics to NX16-013.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxRollback -Category NXcc filters journal entries by tweak ID prefix, then applies the same reverse-order, only-if-ours, verified restoration.
tweaks.proposedState: All journaled changes of the category restored.

verify.procedure: Rollback result: every category target restored or explicitly reported diverged/failed.

tweaks.name: Profile rollback
tweaks.description: Restores all journaled changes applied under a given user profile (e.g. P1).
tweaks.objective: Scope 3 of 4: undo a profile's applied set without touching others.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxRollback -Profile Pn filters journal entries recorded with that profile tag at apply time, then applies the same verified restoration. Combined-profile applications are respected: an entry journaled under P1+P3 is included in either profile's rollback only when no other recorded profile still claims it (explicit resolution prompt otherwise).
tweaks.proposedState: The profile's journaled changes restored; shared entries resolved explicitly, never silently.

verify.procedure: Rollback result: profile-tagged targets restored; shared-target resolutions logged.

tweaks.name: Full NEXTRIX rollback
tweaks.description: Restores every journaled change NEXTRIX has made on the machine, newest first.
tweaks.objective: Scope 4 of 4: complete, order-aware, verified restoration.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxRollback -All: full journal replay in reverse, integrity-gated (refuses to run on a tampered journal), only-if-ours, per-step journaled and verified. On success the journal is marked restoredVerifiedUtc and capture re-arms (fresh stock capture on next apply). This is the answer to the platform's missing uninstall (ADR-006).
tweaks.proposedState: All journaled NEXTRIX changes restored; journal marked verified-restored.

verify.procedure: Rollback result: restored/diverged/failed summary; manifest carries restoredVerifiedUtc.

sideEffects: Long-running on large journals; progress is reported per step.

tweaks.name: Owner support-bundle export
tweaks.description: One-click export: hardware report, build report, journal summary, health checks - scrubbed of machine identifiers.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a complete, privacy-safe evidence bundle for manual testing and issue reports.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Bundles Get-NxHardwareReport/Get-NxBuildReport JSON, a journal summary (tweak IDs, timestamps, results - never secrets), optional DISM/SFC reports, into a zip with machine identifiers scrubbed (computer name, SIDs, serials). Nothing is uploaded - the file lands where the owner chooses (XOS diagnostic-ZIP pattern, r1).
tweaks.proposedState: Scrubbed support bundle at owner-chosen path.

verify.procedure: Bundle exists, contains the listed reports, scrub list applied.

sideEffects: Writes one zip file to the owner-chosen location.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (Export PC Specs; diagnostic ZIP uploads nothing)
